subject: Air-gapped deployment: operator on-call simulations & maintenance scenarios

Subject: Air-gapped deployment: operator on-call simulations & maintenance scenarios

Maya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward a narrow pilot of the air-gapped bundle at our primary site, our security and ops teams want to run two types of exercises before sign-off: a) an operator on-call simulation (tabletop + live run through) and b) a maintenance/patch window dry run that covers offline patching, KMS key rotation, and operator handoff.

Can you provide:
- A concise checklist for the on-call simulation (roles, scripted incidents, expected operator actions)
- The maintenance dry-run steps and time estimates for each phase
- Any constraints on remote troubleshooting (what telemetry you can share, jump-host requirements)
- A sample SLA-exception template we can use to approve short maintenance windows during pilot

Also please include network diagrams and any attachments you expect our network/security teams to review. Our timeline goal is to run the tabletop next Thursday and the live simulation the week after. Is that feasible from your side?

Appreciate it — Olivia

--
Olivia Grant
VP, Infrastructure Operations

olivia.grant@helixhealth.com

Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: operator on-call simulations & maintenance scenarios

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely support both exercises and have attached a draft checklist (operator-sim-checklist.xlsx) and a high-level network diagram (network-diagram.pdf). I've outlined the proposed approach below so your teams can review quickly.

Proposed sequence (tabletop -> live):
1) Tabletop (60–90m) — participants: Helix ops lead, Helix SOC, Redwood oncall engineer, Redwood program manager. Scripted incidents: control-plane failover, node OOM, patch rollback scenario. Expected outcome: operator follows runbook, validates KV cache restore and model version pin fallback.
2) Live simulation (3–4 hours) — dry run of maintenance window:
   - Pre-checks (30m): backups, local telemetry snapshot, operator credentials verified.
   - Offline patch window (60–90m): apply offline package, run integrity checks, verify model artifacts.
   - KMS rotation (15–30m): rotate keys in customer KMS, confirm decryption of cached artifacts.
   - Post-validation (30–45m): smoke tests, latency checks, read-only verification with synthetic traffic.
3) Operator handoff & postmortem (30m) — ensure runbook updates and action items captured.

Operational constraints and notes:
- Remote troubleshooting: For air-gapped pilots we provide only pull-based telemetry (aggregated logs + checksum manifests). No outbound SSH. Any live debug sessions must be run via customer-controlled jump-host or via recorded trace bundles we produce.
- Required operator privileges: operator account with role: 'deploy-operator' (ability to trigger package install, restart services, rotate KMS pointers). We will provide temporary elevated tokens for the simulation window and advise immediate rotation post-exercise.
- Estimated incident-to-resolution SLA for simulated failover: 30–90 minutes depending on scenario complexity; we will run three scripted incidents to validate median time.

Attached: operator-sim-checklist.xlsx (checklist + sample scripts), network-diagram.pdf (high-level topology). We'll follow up with an SLA exception template — Irene is drafting that now.

Proposed dates:
- Tabletop: Thu, 04 Dec 2026 10:00–11:30 PST
- Live sim: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 08:00–12:00 PST (flexible)

If those work, we'll lock resources and circulate an attendee list.

Best,

Olivia / Maya — a few technical clarifications from the runbook perspective (copying text from the checklist for clarity):

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 11:05 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Offline patch window (60–90m): apply offline package, run integrity checks, verify model artifacts.

Technical detail items to confirm with your infra team:
- Image delivery: offline packages are distributed as signed tarballs. Customer environment must provide an isolated staging host that can receive the tarball via an approved USB or air-gap transfer process; we validate signatures locally.
- Network policies: During the simulation the cluster should be allowed DNS-only egress to our verification endpoint on port 443 if you opt-in to telemetry ingestion; otherwise, all telemetry will be uploaded manually via secure media.
- Jump-host: if Helix requires live troubleshooting, we recommend a single hardened jump-host in DMZ with restricted egress; Redwood will connect only to that host via your temporary ephemeral certs. No persistent access is requested.
- Telemetry retention: for the pilot we retain simulation traces for 30 days; production customers can request different windows in contract.

If Helix wants to shorten individual sub-steps to fit a tighter maintenance window, we can provide a condensed checklist but recommend keeping the integrity and KMS steps intact — they are the highest risk.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: SLA exception draft + tabletop facilitator notes

Hi all — drafting an SLA-exception template and facilitator notes for the tabletop. Attached: sla-exception-request.docx (customer-facing draft you can adapt). Key callouts in the draft:
- Exception window: up to 6 hours for pilot maintenance events; automatic rollback clause at 90 minutes unless a joint decision is made to extend.
- Responsibility matrix: customer is responsible for physical media transfer and KMS control; Redwood responsible for signed artifacts and runbook execution.
- Escalation path: Redwood oncall -> Redwood engineering lead -> Helix oncall -> Helix engineering manager (contact info table in doc).

Tabletop facilitator agenda (30–45m):
1) Introductions & goals (5m)
2) Walk through scripted incident A (failover) and B (patch failure) (20m)
3) Validate decision points and handoff triggers (10m)
4) Capture actions and close (5m)

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHelixOncallSim (has the checklist and diagram) and JIRA INF-734 for tracking follow-ups.
